pce.why: rdpmc at CPL 3 needs CR4.PCE = 1; the SDM only defines the bit, the declared CPU's cpuid does not state it, the WDK 7.1 constants name no PCE bit and Wine 9.0 has no rdpmc case

tsd.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr intercepts only the 0F opcodes ['0x20', '0x21', '0x22', '0x23'], so rdtsc (0F 31) runs in user mode; consistent with the owner's decision that rdtsc reads the platform timer

umip.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 2.5 CR4.UMIP: the bit is reserved (setting it is #GP) unless CPUID.(EAX=07H,ECX=0):ECX[2] is enumerated; the declared CPU's max basic leaf is 4 (ports/fnv-nx/lift/rt/cpumodel.c FNVL_MAX_BASIC @ b5af46461e81), below 7, so there is no leaf 7 and CR4.UMIP is 0

initial.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: the initial thread context, context.EFlags

iopl.source: bits 12-13 of the initial EFLAGS (Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6)

iopl_user_modifiable.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): EFLAGS_USER_SANITIZE = 0x3F4DD7, the EFLAGS bits user code can set; bits 12-13 are not in it

idtr_limit.why: the number of gates of the OS's IDT is not stated by a pinned source (the SDM allows 256 entries at most)

other_vectors.why: no pinned source says whether Windows 7 has a ring-3 gate at any other vector; Wine 9.0 handles only these

int_ring3.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: handle_interrupt cases ['0x29', '0x2d']; segv_handler / trap_handler map ['TRAP_x86_BPTFLT', 'TRAP_x86_OFLOW'] to #OF / #BP

ds.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

es.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

fs.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

gs.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

ss.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3; ss needs a writable data segment, not the null selector

undecided.why: the ring-3 code descriptor's readable bit is not stated in a pinned source, so whether es/ds/fs/gs may load it is undecided

cs.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_R3_CODE = 0x18 (the ring-3 code segment) | RPL_MASK 3

ds.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_R3_DATA = 0x20 (the ring-3 data segment) | RPL_MASK 3

es.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_R3_DATA = 0x20 (the ring-3 data segment) | RPL_MASK 3

fs.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_R3_TEB = 0x38 (the TEB's segment) | RPL_MASK 3

gs.why: no pinned source gives the initial gs of a Windows 7 user thread (Wine loads the host's gs, the WDK has no KGDT constant for it)

ss.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_R3_DATA = 0x20 (the ring-3 data segment) | RPL_MASK 3

tr.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_TSS (the task state segment selector)

sgdt.why: the GDT base and limit of the OS are kernel values with no documented fixed value and no pinned source

sidt_base.why: the IDT base is a kernel address with no documented fixed value and no pinned source

sldt.why: no pinned source states the LDTR of a process that has no LDT

cpumodel.origin: the declared CPU's cpuid (CPUREF), L3a rt/cpumodel.c
